{{Short description|Hong Kong chemist}}
{{distinguish|text=Hong Kong University law professor [[Albert Chen]]}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Chen (surname)|Chan]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Albert Sun-Chi Chan''' ({{zh|t=陳新滋|p=Chén Xīnzī|j={{kCantonese|陳新滋}}|first=j}}; born 30 October 1950) is a [[Hong Kong]] chemist. He is a professor of chemistry and [[traditional Chinese medicine]]. He has served as a vice-president of the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]] (PolyU) and the president of [[Hong Kong Baptist University]] (HKBU).

==Career==
Chan began his professional career in chemistry in 1979 at [[Monsanto]] in the United States. He moved back to Asia in 1992 to serve as a visiting expert at [[National Taiwan University]], and then returned to Hong Kong in 1994 to take up the position of chairman of PolyU's Department of Applied Biology and Chemical Engineering.<ref name="HKPUAAM2007">{{cite news|url=http://www.hkpolyuaa.org.au/newsletter/2007AGMComplete.pdf |title=Special Welcoming of Prof. Albert Chan |work=Hong Kong Polytechnic University (Australia) Association Magazine |year=2007 |access-date=2013-04-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017092016/http://www.hkpolyuaa.org.au/newsletter/2007AGMComplete.pdf |archive-date=2013-10-17 }}</ref> While teaching at PolyU, he also pursued academic interests in [[mainland China]], becoming the first dean of [[Sun Yat-sen University]]'s School of Pharmaceutical Sciences and later the first director of the State Key Laboratory of Medicine and Molecular Pharmacology in [[Shenzhen]].<ref name="SCMP20091020">{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/article/695970/baptist-u-names-head-process-draws-fire|first=Austin|last=Chiu|title=Baptist U names head, but process draws fire|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=2009-10-20|access-date=2013-04-20}}</ref> He was named a fellow of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 2001.<ref name="CRN20091019"/> He held his PolyU departmental chairmanship until 2007, when he became the dean of the university's Faculty of Applied Science and Textiles and the vice-president for Research and Development.<ref name="HKPUAAM2007"/>

In 2009, Chan was named as the president of [[Hong Kong Baptist University]] for a five-year term to begin in July 2010.<ref name="CRN20091019">{{cite news|url=http://www.chinareviewnews.com/doc/1011/0/9/1/101109149.html?coluid=7&kindid=0&docid=101109149|title=陳新滋獲委任為香港浸會大學校長 (Chan Sun-Chi appointed as Hong Kong Baptist University president)|work=China Review News|date=2009-10-19|access-date=2013-04-09|archive-date=2018-10-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022184943/http://www.chinareviewnews.com/doc/1011/0/9/1/101109149.html?coluid=7&kindid=0&docid=101109149|url-status=dead}}</ref> His selection as university president drew criticisms from faculty and students for the opacity of the selection process. Search committee chairman Wilfred Wong Ying-wai stated that Chan was clearly the best candidate among the six who had been short-listed, and defended the committee's decision not to involve students in the selection process.<ref name="SCMP20091020"/> Chan's goals for his term as president included improving HKBU to become one of the world's top 200 universities and developing the university's traditional Chinese medicine research capabilities.<ref name="SCMP20091020"/><ref name="AppleDaily20091020">{{cite news|url=http://hk.apple.nextmedia.com/news/art/20091020/13331618|title=浸大新校長 陳新滋：有政治壓力將辭職 (New Baptist U. president Chan Sun-Chi: if there is any political pressure I will resign)|work=[[Apple Daily]]|date=2009-10-20|access-date=2013-04-20}}</ref> In 2013, he became involved in a high-profile dispute with the Town Planning Board over the zoning of land near the university; HKBU had made plans as early as 2009 to use the land to build a traditional Chinese medicine [[teaching hospital]], while the government hoped to sell the land to real estate developers to build high-end flats. Chan threatened to resign from his post to protest the government's decision.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/article/1147483/baptist-university-president-threatens-quit-over-land-use|title=Baptist University president threatens to quit over land use|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=2013-02-10|access-date=2013-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/article/1180382/baptist-university-boss-spars-ko-wing-man-over-school-site|first=Olga|last=Wong|title=Baptist University boss spars with Ko Wing-man over school site|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=2013-03-06|access-date=2013-04-20}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Chan was born in [[Taishan, Guangdong|Taishan]], [[Guangdong]]. He moved to Hong Kong at the age of 14, where he worked hard at memorising English vocabulary in order to catch up with other students and eventually achieved excellent academic results, earning him a scholarship to pursue higher education in Japan.<ref name="Mingpao20100108">{{cite news|url=http://life.mingpao.com/htm/jupas/cfm/Jupas1.cfm?File=uguide2010_18.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130427052619/http://life.mingpao.com/htm/jupas/cfm/Jupas1.cfm?File=uguide2010_18.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-04-27 |title=陳新滋：學習不能孤軍作戰 (Chan Sun-Chi: studying is not a battle that can be fought alone) |work=[[Ming Pao]] |date=2010-01-08 |access-date=2013-04-20 }}</ref> There, he enrolled in [[International Christian University]] in [[Tokyo]], where he earned a B.S. in chemistry in 1975.<ref name="CRN20091019"/> He then went on to the [[University of Chicago]], where he defended a doctoral thesis on [[asymmetric hydrogenation]] in 1979.<ref>{{harvnb|Chan|1979}}</ref>

While living in the US, he naturalised as a citizen; he later [[renunciation of United States citizenship|renounced U.S. citizenship]] in 2001 after being named an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.<ref name="AppleDaily20091020"/><ref>{{Cite web|date=2002-04-22|title=Quarterly Publication of Individuals, Who Have Chosen To Expatriate, as Required by Section 6039G|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2002/04/22/02-9801/quarterly-publication-of-individuals-who-have-chosen-to-expatriate-as-required-by-section-6039g|access-date=2020-07-23|website=Federal Register}}</ref> He was named a [[Justice of the Peace]] of Hong Kong on 30 June 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.info.gov.hk/jp/eng/2012_jp_lists.pdf|title=2012 Justice of the Peace Appointments|work=Info.gov.hk|date=2012-06-30|access-date=2013-04-20|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083145/http://www.info.gov.hk/jp/eng/2012_jp_lists.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
